The text discusses the impending end of the E-Rate program and its impact on school districts. It highlights the financial burden of maintaining network equipment beyond its lifecycle and the cybersecurity risks associated with unsecured perimeter hardware. The text argues that limiting or eliminating E-Rate funding would directly convert an operational affordability challenge into a significant cybersecurity and data privacy crisis.

The text discusses the impact of limiting or ending the E-Rate program on school districts and students. It highlights the financial challenges and the need to maintain network infrastructure for online safety and educational purposes. The text argues that the core objective of E-Rate should not be concluded as achieved, as network infrastructure is an ongoing operational utility that requires continuous capital investment.
